beats.title: WHAT A CONTRACT IS
beats.vo: A contract is what a tool tells your agent it does. Its name, its parameters, what it promises to touch.
captions: contract = what a tool tells your agent it does
23,617 tools drifted · 6,882 changed a contract field we surface
1,170 of 4,869 servers ever reachable · 3,892 safety-relevant, not confirmed vulnerabilities

beats.title: WHY NOTHING YOU ALREADY HAVE CATCHES IT
beats.vo: Access control answers who may call a tool, not whether it still does what it declared. And a server launched at latest re-resolves every time, so there is nothing pinned to begin with. Where there is, across the remote servers we crawl, nearly three quarters of the drifting tools we could check had only ever changed with the server's version unchanged.
captions: Auth answers WHO may call.
Not WHETHER it still does what it declared.
/scan: "4,982 of 6,882 drifting tools have only ever changed with their declared version unchanged, where version evidence exists"

beats.title: PIN, DIFF, THREE OUTCOMES
beats.vo: The gate pins each tool's contract on first sight, then diffs it on every call. An added optional parameter proceeds without interrupting you. A change that would surprise your agent stops the call on your machine. When only behaviour could settle the question, the gate refuses to guess. It returns inconclusive, and the call still stops.
captions: Pin on first sight.
added-optional-param → proceeds · baseline re-pinned automatically
Review · Re-pin · Reject
mcpindex.ai/install

beats.title: TWO LIMITS, STATED PLAINLY
beats.vo: Two limits. If a tool was already lying when you pinned it, the gate pins the lie: your baseline is what you first saw. And a read only hint is self-declared, so behind some of those two hundred and five was a maintainer fixing a wrong label. The gate cannot tell which, so it stops the call instead of judging it.
captions: The baseline is what you first saw.
readOnlyHint is self-declared. A maintainer fixing a wrong label flips the same bit.
three outcomes, not two: PROCEED · HOLD · INCONCLUSIVE
annotation flip → INCONCLUSIVE · fail-closed · the call still stops

beats.title: WHAT IT IS, AND IS NOT
beats.vo: It is a contract diff, not a safety verdict. It tells you what changed, never that the change is safe. What makes that worth having is where it sits: in the call path, so an advisory judgment still stops the call.
captions: Contract-diff, not a safety verdict.
Advisory judgment. In-path HOLD.
Deterministic diff. No model in the default path.
Your host. Zero credential custody.

beats.title: INSTALL
beats.vo: The gate is two commands. If you run MCP servers in Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or five other hosts, the wizard rewrites each host config to route your servers through it, and marks every entry it touches so one command unwires it. Restart, and the first tools list pins every tool you have. Then nothing happens. That silence is the gate working. The next thing you see is your first hold.
captions: no pipe-to-shell

beats.vo: Building your own agent? One line wraps an MCP session: the same diff and the same hold, in your code, with a pin you point at wherever you keep it. Turn on result scanning and it also reads what comes back before your agent does. Check the licence before you ship.
